messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Production streaming p99 spike on /v1/stream (region: us-west1). Alert: p99 > 1.8s for 10m. Affected service: runtime-decode. Incident ID: INC-2026-0421.

Devon H: ack. I'm on it. grabbing dashboard -> https://grafana.internal/redwood/explore?panel=streaming-decode-p99

Devon H: quick context — we're seeing streaming stalls and long tail on decode kernels. Recent kernel/compile rollout 4h ago (kernel-image: rtd-2026-03-15-kt1). Any recent config flips? @Matt L we pushed TRT8 flash-optimizations earlier today?

Matt L: yep pushed a toolchain update and enabled flashattn micro-kernel flag in the runtime build at ~171200. I flagged it as safe on unit tests but not wide perf.

Matt L: observed symptoms match a compilepath regression: continuous batches get a tail spike when KV cache misses and attention fallback hits a slower kernel. p95 mostly fine, p99 jumps.

Devon H: current SLO: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 800ms. Current: p95=220ms, p99=2.4s on v1/stream, throughput okay. Customer impact: streaming stalls visible for long responses (~>2s chunks). CS: any high-severity customer alerts? @CS Lead?

CS Lead: we have 2 customers (enterprise) reporting timeouts in the last 30m. Both are using Dedicated + streaming. They're seeing token flow pauses. No outage but degraded UX.

Devon H: mitigation plan (short term):
- roll back kernel image on a few suspect nodes (canary)
- route traffic for Dedicated streaming to legacy model-quantized variant (model:v1-legacy)
- reduce batch size for streaming to avoid hitting fallback path (runtime flag: --max-batch=8)
- enable aggressive prefix KV caching for hot paths

Matt L: rolling back kernel on one pool now. Command:```bash
kubectl set image ds/runtime-worker runtime-worker=registry.redwood/release/rtd-2026-03-14-kt9 --namespace=prod-us-west1
```

Matt L: also applying runtime env override on fleet to force legacy attention for suspect model:```json
{"RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION":"1"}
```

Devon H: thumbs. Applying routing change to move dedicated traffic to legacy model (will preserve latency for Dedicated customers). Doing canary deploy for 5% traffic now.

sre-bot: Deploy started: canary 5% -> 10 nodes. CI checks passed.

10m later — Devon H: early signal — p99 on canary nodes dropped to ~700ms, overall cluster p99 down to 1.1s (from 2.4s). Streaming stalls reduced on canary.

Matt L: looks like rollback helps. Hypothesis: new compile path introduced a regression in FlashAttention path that only triggers on certain sequence length distributions and KV cache miss patterns (seen in long streaming sessions). Will dig into assembly/kernels.

Devon H: good. Next actions:
- continue canary rollback + ramp to 50% if steady
- open incident ticket + set severity to Sev2 (customer impact but no full outage)
- capture perf traces from affected nodes (traces: /traces/1758456789)
- start a snapshot of compiler flags and binary artifacts for root cause (save toolchain build IDs)

Matt L: starting a parallel repro: running a synthetic streaming workload with the same token length distribution and KV miss ratio (script: tools/repro/streaming-tail.sh). If we can reproduce deterministically we'll file a regression PR to the compiler team.

Devon H: tagging @Zara P as next on-call for handoff in 30m. Summary for handoff: rollback in progress, canary positive, routing to model:v1-legacy for Dedicated, mitigation flags applied (--max-batch=8, RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION=1). Key links: Grafana dashboards, traces, deploy link.

Zara P: thanks — taking over at 1758457900. I'll monitor p95/p99 and continue ramp if stable. If any increase in error rates or queue growth, I'll escalate.

SRE Pager: Incident created: https://tracker.internal/INC-2026-0421. Owner: Devon H. Sev2.

Devon H: note for postmortem — need to add a perf-gate in CI for streaming-tail distributions and add a canary job that exercises long streaming sessions before rolling compile flags.

Matt L: discovered an additional runtime flag that was toggled by the new build: `ATTN_USE_TRT_FLASH=1` — this combined with `--enable-kernel-autochunk` seems to create a slow path on cache misses. We'll revert the flag in the build and run perf tests.

Zara P: mitigation status update (1758458050): canary ramped to 30%, cluster p99 now 620ms, p95 210ms. No new customer escalations in the last 15m. Proceeding to 60% ramp in 10m if stable.

Devon H: handoff complete. Leaving the incident with Zara for monitoring & next steps: isolate regression, revert build flag, and schedule a controlled redeploy with extended perf tests. I'll draft the incident timeline and assign root-cause tasks.

CS Lead: communicating to affected customers: "we've implemented a mitigation that reduced tail latency; engineering is investigating a kernel compile regression and will follow up with RCA."

Matt L: opened internal regression ticket: REG-2026-778. Attaching traces and a repro script.

Devon H: final note: if rollback doesn't fully normalize p99 after full ramp, fallback is to put streaming on low-latency hardware pool (dedicated-ll) and continue investigation offline.

sre-bot: Update: mitigation succeeded on canary; monitoring watching for 1h.

Devon H: closing initial on-call thread, follow-up postmortem to be scheduled. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
